Central Palace, Market Enclosure, Imperial Seat, Seven Dukes, Sun Star, Imperial Couch, Great Horn, Sombre Establishment, Supreme Palace, Five Emperors, Crown Prince, Bright Hall, Chariot Axis, Three Terraces, Five Chariots, Various Kings, Moon Star, Weaver Girl, Establishment Star, Celestial Record—seventeen seats and the twenty-eight lodges—are ranked before the front row.

差在前列 means ranked in the front row, not before it; the literal “before the front row” adds a false preposition.

On the first upper day of the first month, prayer for grain sacrifices to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, with Emperor Gaozu as associated deity; the Five Emperors stand on the steps of the four directions.

On the first xin day of the first month, at the prayer-for-grain sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, Emperor Gaozu, the Divine Yao Emperor, serves as associated recipient; the Five Emperors occupy the steps in the four directions.
上辛 is the first xin day, 神堯皇帝 is the Divine Yao Emperor, and 配 denotes the associated recipient.
On the day when Earth is king in late summer, sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor, with the Chariot Axis clan as associated deity; the Queller Star and Queen Earth are positioned as for the Red Emperor.
On the day when Earth is king in late summer, sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor, with Xuanyuan as associated deity; the Queller Star and Queen Earth are positioned as for the Red Emperor.
軒轅氏 is the personal/clan name Xuanyuan paired with the Yellow Emperor; “Chariot Axis clan” is a star-seat calque, not this associated deity.

On the day when Earth is king in the last month of summer, sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor, with the Chariot Axis clan as associated deity; the positions of the Queller Star and Queen Earth are as for the Red Emperor.

At the wax sacrifice to the hundred spirits, the Bright Luminary and Night Luminary are on the altar; the Divine Farmer and Yiyi each on his altar; Houji east of the altar; the Five Officials and field directors each in his direction; the Five Stars, twelve chronograms, twenty-eight lodges, directional mountains and garrisons, seas and rivers, mountains, forests, rivers, marshes, hills, mounds, plains, wetlands, and wells and springs each on altars in his direction; dragon, unicorn, vermilion bird, zouyu, dark warrior, scaled, feathered, naked, furred, shelled, water embankments, wards, postal markers, watch huts, yutu, and cat each behind altars in his direction.
